Results.ReviewText:
I purchased my Timberline 1300 four years ago, and overall it has been an excellent grill.

Pros:
It delivers outstanding results with beef, chicken, and turkey, and it truly takes much of the guesswork out of cooking. The build quality is impressive — the grill feels extremely sturdy and well-made. Despite its weight, it is surprisingly easy to move around. Most importantly, the cooking performance has been consistently excellent.

Cons:
After approximately 1.5 to 2 years, rust began developing on the wheels, the bottom edge of the lid, and the rear smoke plate became heavily rusted as well.

Another concern, however, is the app and Wi-Fi connectivity. While the app has great potential, it frequently loses connection to my phone and often requires reconnecting to the Wi-Fi network. I have a strong wireless mesh setup with 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz coverage, with reliable signal even across the street, so network strength is not the issue. Because of the repeated connectivity problems, I eventually stopped using the app altogether.

That said, I have no complaints about the grill’s actual cooking performance — it truly is fantastic. However, the app reliability, Wi-Fi connectivity, and rust issues definitely need to be addressed.
Results.Title: Timberline 1300 4 Year review

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thanks for your feedback on the Timberline 1300. The Timberline series is a fully insulated line of pellet grills, specifically designed to work well in a variety of climates, including colder ones. While extreme conditions may still result in an extended startup, once the Timberline gets going, it should hold temperature very well if there are no other factors involved. As for the grease fire and pellets burning in the auger tube (backburn), these can be mitigated by regular maintenance. For grease fires to occur, there really needs to be a substantial buildup of grease, which can actually ignite even if the grill is set to lower temperatures. The same can go for backburn, with an excess accumulation of ash in the firepot preventing proper airflow, which then causes the fire to burn in the only direction that there is enough oxygen - back through the auger tube. Of course, there may be other details specific to your situation, but we were unable to find any contacts with Customer Service based on your attached email. If you haven’t yet discussed your experience with Traeger Support, please reach out to us when you are with the grill, and we will be happy to look at the situation more closely.
ClientResponses.Name: Traeger Grills

Results.ReviewText:
I’ve been using my Timberline 1300 for a few years now. It’s a decent smoker and does its job well when it works. If you’re thinking about grilling on this thing though, go somewhere else. If you live in a colder climate and want to grill year round, this grill is not for you. 

This grill is also not for you if you’re on a time crunch. The grill takes absolutely forever to get up to temp (if it actually even makes it to the temp you set it to). Then, good luck holding that temp once you put in your meat. They’ll blame it on poor quality pellets, even when you’re using a fresh bag of their own. 

If you’re lucky enough to get to a high temp, then you get to see how easy it is to start a grease fire in the thing. The fire usually likes to then work its way down the auger, burning up all the pellets along the way, so be ready to empty your hopper so they all don’t go up in flames. 

With the high temps then comes peeling paint and inevitable rust! Fun! Even if you keep it covered religiously when it’s not in use, you won’t escape this either. 

I hope Traeger is embarrassed charging as much as it does for this grill, because I’m sure embarrassed that I purchased one.
Results.Title: If you enjoy headaches, this thing is for you!

ClientResponses.Response: Hello, and thanks for sharing your experience with the Timberline 1300. Although some grease will stay on the drip tray during a cook, the majority should drain out to the trough without pooling. However, the reason that this might not be happening on your Timberline could be directly related to the foil wrapped over the tray. As seen in one of your photos, the foil is raised in some areas, which has created a wall that has obstructed grease flow out of the grill. Since it is very difficult to apply foil flat, and keep it that way during a cook, it is recommended that a tray liner is used instead, which is thicker than foil, so it will maintain its shape better, and remain flatter on the tray. Either that, or you can try using the grill without covering the pan at all, though this will make cleanup a little more time consuming.

Then exceed set temperature by 30 degrees above set point for 30 minutes. Called Traeger and after hour and a half they said they would send me a new controller. You should have it before the weekend (June 23). Still haven’t received it. 
Traeger customer service said to keep using the grill until the controller comes. 
Used the grill on June 21. It goes up in smoke and back burns through the auger into the hopper. 
And yes, I use Traeger pellets, it’s cleaned more frequently than required, I sift my pellets, the grill is level.
For a grill this expensive, it should work a lot better than this. 
I wish I never sold my Bronson 20. 
My PTG that is 15 years old works better than this thing.

Results.OriginalProductName: Timberline 850 Pellet Grill - In Store Only
Results.ReviewText:
The Timberline 850 makes grilling and cooking easy to do with consistently delicious results.  It smokes meat much better than some critics would have you believe (I say that comparing it to my Big Green Egg).  Temperatures are easy to adjust and once you set a temperature, the Traeger does a great job of maintaining the desired temperature even in 20-degree weather.  

Technology:  The WiFi feature works flawlessly.  If you have a solid home WiFi network (no interference or distance issues) then you will absolutely love the ability to control your cook from your phone.  

Durability:  I regularly clean the outside of my grill and keep an eye on the fire pot although it hasn't ever needed cleaning (despite the reminder message I'm greeted with every time I start the Traeger--it's a standard message you'll see when the system is booting up).  The very back metal plate of the grill showed signs of paint peeling, but that's my fault--I had the unit too close to my brick wall at 500 degrees for many hours.  A light sanding and some flat black paint took care of that little mistake.  

Customer Service:  I had an initial warranty claim (interior metal shield was warped upon delivery) and Traeger got me a replacement in two days without issue.  The rep was very knowledgable and did a good job handling the issue.  

While I do like my Egg for some types of cooking, I use my Timberline 850 more often.  There is no doubt that if I had to choose one grill it would be a Traeger.  I easily get 85-90% of the quality results of the Egg 100% of the time--and all I have to do is push a button.  

This is my second Traeger in 10 years and I highly recommend it.

Results.ReviewText:
I have had the timberline 850 for two years now and sad to say it just ok as I love to cook, especially grilling and had much higher hopes for this grill.  My single biggest issue is keeping it clean. Anyone that knows anything about grilling knows it all starts with a clean grill and this grill is ridulously tedious to clean.  The way its designed there are so many nooks and crannies that either pellet dust, grease, or both get in places you would never expect and clean up takes forever.  I have had several weber grills over the years and the primary concern there is keeping the grates clean but with the Timberline 850 its way more than keeping grates clean. I spend two hours cleaning it for every 6-8 hours of cooking.  

I keep my grill in the garage when its not being used to keep it protected and have learned how critical it is to make sure its perfectly level because even if its just off slightly in a way the reduces the juice and grease flow the clean up is even more difficult and time consuming.  The drip pan covers need to be installed perfectly or they too will restrict the grease flow and create additional clean up issues.  It just seems to be a poor design for a high end grill.  I have a shop vac dedicated to cleaning this grill and even with that to clean it right you have to remove quite a few screws to remove interior covers to adequately g clean the nooks and crannies. The best feature is that is great a holding a temperature and contolling it with the wi-fire app is very convenient.  Even so, I find myself using my old charcoal weber grill more and more simply becuase I dont want have to deal with the clean up of theTraeger.  I pretty much only use the Traeger when I am cooking a large amount of food for 6 people or more to justify the cleaning of the grill.  I guess I am not the only one that feels this way as the clean up issue seems to have been addressed with the newer models.  If you are consideing buying a Treager, I strongly suggest you look at the new model with the EZ clean pot to avoid a situation like mine where you spend alot of money on a grill that is only used selectivelydue due to the hassle of cleaning it.

Results.ReviewText: Apologies ahead of time for the rant, but I feel it's a little overdue. Purchased the Timberline 850, and within a few smokes I noticed the powder-coating on the outside corner of the barrel beginning to bubble and fleck off. There were also the very beginning signs of surface rust, so I contacted customer support. I was told that their warranty doesn't cover paint/cosmetic damage, and only rust if there is an actual hole; and finally that I should just cover it up with a high-temp paint. First of all, for a +$2k smoker and such an acclaimed rugged outdoor appliance, I shouldn't have to touch up anything on it, especially within such a short period of time and after such ginger use. Secondly, it clearly states on your website that the warranty would be voided if I were to apply paint, as suggested by their CS team member. I clean all of my T's regularly, they have never had a flare up, and all of them, even my 850's short life, have been placed under a cover when not being used. Clearly the powder-coating wasn't applied correctly, thus the delaminating of it already And by the time a physical hole actually does rust through the barrel, the warranty will have lapsed. I'm disappointed that they don't just address the problem and make it right. I've owned many Traegers myself, and purchased a few for family and friends solely because of their CS team and willingness to help out a fellow BBQ enthusiast. Quality has gone down and their customer service isn't what it use to be. There was a time when Traeger would have bent over backwards for their customers, but I believe that time has come and gone.

Results.OriginalProductName: Timberline 1300 Pellet Grill - In Store Only
Results.ReviewText:
The Timberline 1300 has ruined my Traeger experience.  I purchased a Pro 22 originally and absolutely loved it.  I cooked everything on that grill.  I hosted, neighborhood cookouts with 50 plus people, having to cook items ahead to manage with the smaller grill.  It was awesome, I was your typical Traeger fanatic always talking about my grill and probably have sold 10 to family and friends.  

Traeger released the new D2 models and I eventually went all in on the 1300.  It has been nothing but problems from day one with grease fires.  I keep the grill clean and have never had issues like this with the much cheaper Pro 22.  The issue is the Timberline series has a very poor grease management system.  They have little slope on this model's drip tray.  Then there is a 34" wide grease trough along the front of the grill to catch all the grease from that tray.  Whenever you cook above 300 with this model, you run the risk of a grease fire.  

It's really unfortunate because I never had any issues with the Pro 22.  I bought a Pro 575 more recently, and have had no issues with that one either.  

Sort these reviews and read all the fire complaints.  It's a major issue and essentially keeps me from using the grill for anything but smoking.  It's a real shame to have bought the top of the line model at the time and not be able to rely on it and use it.  I highly recommend if you want a Traeger, to get the Pro series or Ironwood series.  They are more reliable in my experience.

Almost a month later I'm still waiting on a part or parts to arrive, which may or may not fix the grill. I will be sent a 'How to' fix it guide apparently and would I mind posting the old parts back. I never knew I'm now a Traeger employee fixing their broken grills!!!!?!?!?!?!?!?

Now if this was a £500 grill then I might accept this brush off aftercare.
But not when we're talking close to the £2000 mark.

I think it is both fair and reasonable to expect and be given a like for like exchange.... imagine Mercedes, or Audi asking you to swap over a faulty gearbox on your new car and deliver back the old one.

Results.OriginalProductName: Timberline 1300 Pellet Grill - In Store Only
Results.ReviewText:
Poor quality for the price
a month ago
I have owned my Timberline 1300 for 45 days. I have loved it so far. I have used my grill a handful of times. I clean it after every cook to take care of. I cooked a whole brisket July 4th weekend. It turned out fantastic. 13 hours at 200 degrees, pulled it wrapped in butcher paper for another 5 hours at 250. I also had a pan of all day baked beans on the grill at the same time. When I pulled the brisket I turned the temperature up to 300 to finish the beans. Went in side, came back out later and pulled the beans. Best meal we ever had! Went to clean my grill the next day and the bottom left side of the exterior barrel was all bubbled up. I thought it was grease or condensation. Wiped it off and paint just came peeling off. I spent two hours on the phone with Traeger customer service and got the same pitch everyone else gets. Grease flare up, cosmetic damage, can't help you! This is wrong. How do you sell a grill for $2300.00 that cant with stand heat. I was told my cook data shows when my grill was set to 300 degrees it flared to 400 degrees. So what, the grill can be set to 500 degrees. I have owned high end grills my entire life and have never had paint peel. Now I have a 45 day old very expensive grill that has cosmetic damage I have to live with. Unacceptable, you need a better quality paint with a higher heat tolerance. My request for a new grill was denied. Don't think I can recommend Traeger!

Results.ReviewText: This is a grill I really really wanted to love.  I gave my ‘lil Tex (which I loved) to a friend and upgraded to this model.  After about four cooks with my grill, I noticed the powder coating peeling from the barrel. Notified Traeger, which does have a cool support system via the app, and for some reason they sent me a new backplate, like that would fix the issue.    After paying almost $3k for a grill having paint peeling off the barrel like this, is simply unacceptable.  After months of ‘support’ calls, I finally stopped calling.  They win.  It shouldn't really effect the end result - right?  A year later and this thing is still the gift that keeps on giving.  This grill is the butt of many jokes with my friends.  I have completely ruined great meals at more than one  function.  The biggest issue is the grease evacuation system.  To think that the grease will travel from back to front, then from right to left, then from front to back again is insane.  I spend more time cleaning this machine than cooking on it.  Then to have meals consistently ruined by flare ups, is the final straw.  The only thing worse than the grill is the support.  Talk is cheap when it comes to the 3 yr warranty.
